answer: Bonded stake registries resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock collateral in escrow via a verification bridge prior to network admission. An attacker incurs the verifiable financial cost of illiquid capital and lost yield per identity, whether deploying nodes to coordinate shipping at a jetty or monitor ecology in a meadow. However, this model inherently favors wealthy adversaries who can absorb collateral costs to sponsor multiple fraudulent nodes.
